title: Eighteen Kingdoms
capsule: The Eighteen Kingdoms were the fengjian polities created in 206 BCE by Chu military supremo Xiang Yu after the collapse of the Qin dynasty, parceling the empire among his generals and rival leaders following the Feast at Hong Gate and the burning of Xianyang. Xiang Yu took the title Hegemon-King of Western Chu and assigned the eighteen kingdoms in an attempt to prevent Liu Bang (King of Han) from consolidating power; the arrangement was explicitly designed to reduce Han's territory by confining it to remote Shu-Han and surrounding it with hostile fiefs. The settlement immediately unraveled: within months Liu Bang recrossed the strategic passes, and by 202 BCE he had defeated Xiang Yu at the Battle of Gaixia, ending the Chu-Han Contention and founding the Han dynasty. The Eighteen Kingdoms as a coherent system thus lasted less than four years.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political divisions are documented in Sima Qian's Shiji and Ban Gu's Hanshu, but the precise territories assigned to each king are reconstructed from textual sources alone; archaeological demarcation of boundaries is largely impossible.
